clue.text: Alarm, say, left out? It might wake you in the morning

definitions.text: It might wake you in the morning

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is taken away from the timepiece

parts.note: an alarm is one example of a clock, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a misplaced alarm clock is the thing that rouses them at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from CLOCK. The surface's question mark hints that the definition is a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crowing at dawn is the traditional farmyard wake-up call.

clue.text: Diplomat given a voice when seized by fanatical soldiers

indicators.note: being seized by something means being held inside it, so one pair goes within the other

parts.note: fanatical means mad, wildly enthusiastic
bass is the lowest singing voice
OR is short for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A diplomat finds a voice only once a band of zealous troops grabs him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when seized by' signals the container; 'given' is a link. OR, Other Ranks, is a crossword staple for soldiers, and 'a voice' supplies the article as well as the bass.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior diplomat representing their country abroad.

clue.text: Staff argue regularly and run for supervisor

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word argue

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Employees quarrel now and then and stand for the boss's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'argue', giving AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is someone who oversees and directs staff, a supervisor.

clue.text: Floppy-haired chap — he's installed in second home

parts.note: MO, as in 'half a mo', is a moment or second

indicators.note: being installed in something means being placed inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home or flat
the pronoun he, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A man with unruly hair has moved into a holiday house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed in' signals the container. 'second home' reads like a holiday cottage, but it splits: a moment, then slang for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mophead is an informal name for a person with a thick, shaggy mass of hair.

clue.text: Had horse running across middle part of Aintree: hardly any distance

indicators.note: across means the scrambled letters stretch over and enclose the middle letter
running suggests the letters are set loose and rearranged
middle part of picks out the central letter of the word Aintree

explanation.surface: A racegoer had a horse running on Aintree's course, finishing by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' signals the anagram and 'across' wraps it round the central T of Aintree, the English racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing a short head is the smallest winning margin, so it means a tiny distance.

clue.text: Communist made advances no end, getting elected

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is dropped from the word for made advances

parts.note: to make advances of money is to lend, past tense lent
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A Communist pushed ahead endlessly and won office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops T from LENT, leaving LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin was the leader of the Bolshevik revolution and the founder of Soviet Communism.

clue.text: Twice the collar frayed — strong fabric arrives

indicators.note: frayed suggests the letters are worn apart and reassembled
Twice tells us the word 'the' is used two times over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two worn collars show up, made of sturdy material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles THE, and 'frayed' rearranges THETHE plus COLLAR; 'arrives' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathercloth is a tough coated fabric made to look like leather.

clue.text: A sermon after mass by priest calling for improvement

indicators.note: after tells us the speech comes later than the other pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
Eli is the priest in the biblical Book of Samuel who raised the prophet Samuel
an oration is a formal speech, like a sermon

explanation.surface: Following a service, a priest delivers a sermon urging people to better themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is a crossword favourite for 'priest'; 'calling for' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelioration is the act of making something better, a synonym for improvement.

clue.text: Underground bosses moving east

indicators.note: moving tells us the letter for east shifts to a new position in the word for bosses

parts.note: heads are the bosses of organisations
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Senior managers on the Tube are relocating eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the E of HEADS two places along. 'Underground' tempts as London's Tube but means the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, the realm beneath the earth.

clue.text: Dwelling can be refurbished now he's out

indicators.note: refurbishing renovates and rearranges, so the following words can be remade in new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of he is shortened

explanation.surface: A home could be done up now that the previous occupant has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be refurbished' rearranges NOW HE'S OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A townhouse is a type of house in a town, a residence or dwelling.

clue.text: Female has splurged on toilet cleaners

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: loo is a British informal word for a toilet

indicators.note: splurged suggests spending wildly and messily, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A woman has gone on a spending spree on bathroom-cleaning products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splurged' rearranges HAS into AHS. 'toilet cleaners' looks like one phrase; LOO comes from 'toilet' and 'cleaners' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loofahs are dried gourd sponges used for scrubbing the body clean in the bath.

clue.text: One hit recalled Czech musician

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the two pieces are reversed

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
to ram is to hit forcefully

explanation.surface: Someone struck once remembers a composer from Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns UNIT + RAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinu was a prolific twentieth-century Czech composer.

clue.text: Relevant words on signpost near promontory?

definitions.meaning: relevant means pertinent, directly on the subject
a sign by a headland would direct walkers that way, a headland being a point

explanation.definitionFit: To the point means pertinent; read literally it is a direction towards a headland.

clue.text: Bet linesman has missed header

indicators.note: missing its header means losing the first letter of the poet's name

parts.note: Dante, the Italian poet, is a writer of lines, a linesman

explanation.surface: A gambler notes that a football official failed to win the ball in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has missed header' drops D from DANTE. 'Linesman' looks like a football official but means a poet, a man of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before play in poker, a bet.

clue.text: One with coat pulled up over single item of underwear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece
in a down clue, pulled up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: mac is short for mackintosh, a raincoat
I is the Roman numeral for one
sole means only or single

explanation.surface: Someone yanks their coat up over a lone undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns MAC into CAM; 'over' puts CAMI above SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a loose sleeveless top worn as an undergarment.

clue.text: State's waterway letting a large amount through

indicators.note: letting ... through means the waterway allows the other piece to pass inside it
through completes the phrase, the large amount passing within the waterway

parts.note: a canal is a man-made waterway
tons, or a ton, means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A national waterway allows vast quantities of cargo to pass along it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting' and 'through' together signal the container, split round the large amount. Switzerland's states are cantons, hence the possessive definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonal means belonging to a canton, a state of the Swiss federation, so it is adjectival like a possessive.

clue.text: West safeguarding navy in battle

indicators.note: safeguarding means holding protectively, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Mae West was the American film actress
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Western forces protect the fleet during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safeguarding' signals the container. 'West' looks like a compass point but is the Hollywood actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marne was the site of major First World War battles in France.

clue.text: Creature not entirely fleet, badly needing oxygen

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word for fleet is cut off

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An animal that isn't quite quick on its feet is gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last A of ARMADA. 'fleet' looks like an adjective meaning swift, but is the noun for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Before work, drink a cuppa and encourage disheartened member of school staff

indicators.note: Before tells us the drink comes ahead of the work

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to ply is to work at a trade
a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the central letter, of the word for encourage is removed

parts.note: to cheer someone on is to encourage them

explanation.surface: Ahead of a shift, have a cup of tea and buck up a downcast colleague at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle E of CHEER. A SUPPLY TEACHER covers for an absent teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher is a temporary teacher who fills in for absent staff, so is a school employee.

clue.text: Expected before noon, an upstanding governess

indicators.note: before puts the expected piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: something expected is due

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the word is set upright, read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A respectable governess is due to arrive in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' turns AN into NA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone or governess to girls in a Spanish family.

clue.text: Rubbish conceals hideout … for this creature?

indicators.note: conceals means hides within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a den is a hiding place or lair

explanation.surface: A rubbish heap hides a lair, perhaps for some vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' signals the container. The ellipsis and question mark make the whole clue hint at a rat nesting in a rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat or mouse living in a rubbish heap is a gnawing mammal, the creature meant here.

clue.text: Good books with subjects wise fellow understood

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
themes are subjects or topics
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: Fine books on topics written by a wise man are well grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: OT for 'books' is a crossword convention for the Old Testament; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Got the message is an idiom meaning grasped what was meant.

clue.text: Concerns on radio at last, with up-to-the-minute news coming in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the news goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: re means on the subject of, concerning

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word radio

parts.note: the latest is the most recent news

explanation.surface: Worries about the radio at last broadcasting breaking news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes the final letter of radio and 'coming in' signals the container. 'on' for RE is the Latin 'in the matter of', seen in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Relates to means has to do with, which is what concerns means as a verb.

clue.text: Is university stopping lecturer creating dissension?

indicators.note: stopping means filling a gap, like a stopper in a bottle, so the pieces go inside the lecturer

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a university blocking a lecturer causing internal strife?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' signals the container, as a cork stops a bottle; 'creating' is a link. DON is the Oxbridge word for a lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Disunion is a breakdown of unity, discord or dissension.

clue.text: Popular spot occupied by rogue is unsafe

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: occupied by means filled with, so the rogue goes inside the spot

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat, a place or spot
a cur is a contemptible man, a rogue

explanation.surface: A trendy area taken over by villains is no longer safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' signals the container; 'is' is a link. A see is the area a bishop governs, so it is a spot or place.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means not firmly fixed or protected, which is unsafe.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation in Funchal etc

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Lodgings for holidaymakers are found in Funchal and similar resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'Funchal etc'; Funchal is the capital of Madeira, a fitting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often rented for holidays.

clue.text: Clever, serving a short dram with vermouth

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for dram is cut off

parts.note: a dram is a drop of spirits
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Smart to serve a small whisky with a splash of vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts DROP to DRO; 'serving' is a link. 'dram' wants to be DR, but the letters need DROP trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, a synonym for clever.

clue.text: Lady held up present mother's wrapped

indicators.note: wrapped means enclosed, so mother goes inside the reversed word
in a down clue, held up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: now means the present time
ma is mother, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A lady is delayed because her mother's gift is being wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses the word for present and 'wrapped' signals the container. 'present' looks like a gift but means the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: Woman and lady are near synonyms for an adult female.
